attempts.summary: Made node1 (VyOS) the DNS resolver for the private "lan" network (10.10.10.0/24) it shares with node2 and node3, using PowerDNS Recursor's built-in dns-forwarding service: it answers inventory.internal with node2's lan address (10.10.10.2) via an authoritative-domain record, and forwards all other queries to 1.1.1.1 upstream. node2 and node3 were statically addressed on the lan interface and configured (via NetworkManager) to use node1 (10.10.10.1) as their sole DNS server, with the mgmt-network DHCP-supplied DNS explicitly disabled so resolution unambiguously routes through node1. Everything was implemented and applied idempotently from node4 (the designated control_node) via an Ansible playbook (inventory.ini + site.yml) driving VyOS through a pushed configure-script and RHEL9 clients through community.general.nmcli. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, proving changed boot IDs and full functional/data recovery after each restart, including re-establishing durable (config-persisted) SSH trust from node4 to node1 after discovering VyOS's login reconciler wipes manually-appended authorized_keys.
